Model mechanics

Separate regularized log-linear regressions for 24, 48 and 72-hour offsets. Features: log rainfall, rainfall × regime weights, mean humidity, sea-level pressure, wind, latitude, longitude and month.

Regime weights remain transparent routing proxies, not learned weather diagnoses: four scores begin at 1, with +3 for dry (rain <1 mm), depression-like (pressure <1005 hPa and wind >15 km/h), orographic proxy (elevation >700 m and humidity >75%) and monsoon-like (humidity >75% and rain ≥1 mm). Scores are normalized. Regression coefficients are learned, not hand-set.

Output = max(0, exp(features · coefficients) − 1). No probability or calibrated confidence is inferred. The raw GFS forecast remains visible.

    Indian-network rainfall evaluation

    Exact zeros. Better rainfall errors. Warnings still withheld.

    Test period for the 48h and 72h rows: July 1–September 24, 2026. 2,064 location-days per lead across 24 points. Metrics use ERA5 rain reanalysis as reference. Adjacent sites and repeated weather events are correlated; these are not 2,064 independent storms.

    Update, October 19, 2026: the 24h model now learns on 9,112 grid points. The network grew from 4,000 to 9,112 points across the same 7 regions, and the 24h QM+XGBoost model with its heavy-rain flag was refit on the rebuilt history (2021-03-25 to 2026-08-13; two days with corrupted NOAA files are skipped). The 48h and 72h forecasts still use the v2 ensemble described below. The 24h row (*) is a different evaluation set from the other rows: 546,720 point-days from the 9,112-point network, August 14 to October 12, 2026, all after the fitting period. On it, MAE is 2.82 vs 3.47 for raw GFS and RMSE 7.35 vs 8.61, and the flag finds 890 of 2564 heavy days (raw GFS 550) with 2115 false alarms (raw 1458). Most heavy days are still missed. On 1,083 points never used in fitting (613 of them in new cells), 24h MAE is 2.80 vs 3.56 for raw GFS and false alarms 205 vs 160, with heavy hits 59 vs 39 of 243 for raw GFS. The heavy-flag classifier was refit for precision (no positive-class boosting) and its threshold was set on the same calendar period (August 14 to October 12) of 2021-2025 (300 pre-window days): the lowest flag count that keeps heavy-rain hits at or above the previous model's level in every one of those five seasons, both across all sites and at unseen sites. The test window itself was not used for that choice. On the 4,000 points shared with the previous network and the same days, the new model scores MAE 3.56 vs 3.83 for the previous model. The fitting recipe and settings were selected using this same evaluation period on the older 4,000-point network, so this is not a pristine independent test. Open note on the quality gates: unlike previous releases, this model does not pass the two false-alarm gates used so far. Across all sites it raises 2115 false alarms vs 1664 for the previous model (gate allows at most 1697), and at sites never used in fitting 205 vs 139 (gate allows at most 141), while catching more heavy days (890 vs 839 all-site, 59 vs 54 unseen) and cutting MAE by 8.3% (all-site) and 8.6% (unseen). The owner has explicitly waived the false-alarm gates for this release. The flag still issues no warning or all-clear. Research product, not an official warning.

    Update, October 20, 2026: the 24h correction now covers land areas worldwide (model world-v4). One QM+XGBoost model with a heavy-rain flag, fitted on exactly 1,000,000 land points at 0.125° across 21 regions, history 2021-03-25 to 2026-08-12 (123 fitting days, stratified), evaluated on the following 60 days (2026-08-12 to 2026-10-12, 60.0M point-days; every model choice was made before the evaluation window). Mean absolute error 1.319 mm vs 1.482 for raw GFS (11% better); at cell-held-out points 1.309 vs 1.469. Heavy rain (≥64.5 mm/day): 12,552 hits vs 9,564 for raw GFS (+31%), 38,277 false alarms vs 37,403 (+2.3%). At never-fitted points: hits +33%, false alarms +1.9%. All 21 per-region error gates pass. Open note on the quality gates: one gate of 28 fails: all-site heavy-rain false alarms are 102.34% of raw GFS against a 102% limit (874 extra point-days out of 60M). The unseen-site false-alarm gate passes. The owner has explicitly waived this single gate for this release; all other gates stand. Accuracy is verified against ERA5 0.25° reanalysis truth cells, so the four 0.125° points sharing one cell are not independently verified. Antarctica: precipitation is almost all snow, the rain target is near zero, and the correction is climatologically quiet there. The heavy-rain flag raises the estimate to at least 64.5 mm; it is a research flag, not a warning. Worldwide correction covers 24, 48 and 72-hour leads. Research product, not an official warning.

    Update, October 21, 2026: the worldwide 24h correction is now model world-v6. Same single-stage QM+XGBoost architecture as world-v4, plus five forecast-context inputs: rain over the 3×3 0.125° neighborhood (mean, max, wet fraction) and the two prior GFS runs' rain for the same day. Same fitting period and the identical pinned evaluation window (2026-08-12 to 2026-10-12, 60.0M point-days; every model choice made before the window). MAE 1.298 mm vs 1.482 for raw GFS (12.4% better; world-v4 was 1.319). Heavy rain (≥64.5 mm/day): 12,452 hits vs 9,564 for raw GFS (+30%), and 36,663 false alarms vs 37,403 - 98.0% of raw GFS, below the raw model. At never-fitted points: MAE 1.288 vs 1.469, hits +33%, false alarms 98.5% of raw. All 28 quality gates pass; no waiver was needed for this release. The world-v4 caveats still apply: 0.125° points sharing one ERA5 0.25° truth cell are not independently verified, Antarctica rain is climatologically near zero, and the heavy-rain flag remains a research flag, not a warning. Live neighborhood and prior-run inputs are fetched per location and are approximate; the published scores are archive scores. Research product, not an official warning.

    Update, October 22, 2026: the worldwide correction now covers 48h and 72h leads (models world-l2-v5 and world-l3-v5). Same single-stage QM+XGBoost architecture and the identical pinned evaluation window (2026-08-12 to 2026-10-12, 60.0M point-days per lead; every model choice made before the window except where stated). 48h (world-l2-v5) adds neighborhood rain context and the prior 72h run for the same day: MAE 1.428 mm vs 1.636 for raw GFS (12.7% better); heavy rain (≥64.5 mm/day) 10,089 hits vs 7,118 for raw GFS (+42%); false alarms 40,579 vs 41,274 overall (fewer than raw), and 4,953 vs 5,014 (fewer than raw) at never-fitted points; all 28 quality gates pass on this served configuration. In the western-India and Oceania regions the new model did not beat raw GFS in its checks, so 48h keeps serving raw GFS there, same as before; adding those two regions to the keep-raw list was chosen after the evaluation-window results were seen, disclosed openly (owner-approved October 22, 2026). 72h (world-l3-v5): MAE 1.569 mm vs 1.769 for raw GFS (11.3% better); heavy rain 6,399 hits vs 4,778 (+34%); false alarms 38,885 vs 40,845 overall (fewer than raw), and 4,722 vs 4,873 (fewer than raw) at never-fitted points; all 28 quality gates pass. Where the correction did not beat raw GFS in pre-window checks, the site serves raw GFS: at 72h Antarctica, Middle East, North Asia, Oceania and the west-India network region; at 48h Antarctica, Middle East, Oceania and the west-India network region (the 48h west-India abstention was added after window review, when the correction measured 11.0% worse than raw there; disclosed, not hidden). The world-v6 caveats still apply: 0.125° points sharing one ERA5 0.25° truth cell are not independently verified, and the heavy-rain flag remains a research flag, not a warning. Research product, not an official warning.

    Nightly run log and quality checks

    Live ensemble (48h and 72h): QM+XGBoost weights are 22.5% and 20% for 48h and 72h; the remainder is v1. Exact raw rain zero is forced to zero. In this reused exploratory evaluation the v2 ensemble at 48h beat v1 and raw GFS on both MAE and RMSE. 72h RMSE (17.713) remains worse than raw GFS (17.338), though better than v1 (17.950). This known tradeoff was accepted for this research release. None is near-perfect. Across raw-zero cases, ERA5 references still had at least 1mm on 151 / 142 / 147 days; the gate suppresses those missed-rain cases. ERA5 is reanalysis, not measured gauge truth.

    Training, validation and spatial holdouts

    Fit: January 1–August 31, 2025, 4,374 rows per lead from 18 locations. Original v1 validation: September 2025 plus January–June 2026. Ensemble validation: September 2025–June 2026, 3,798 / 3,798 / 3,762 rows for 24 / 48 / 72h, selecting frozen QM+XGBoost/v1 blend weights. QM and XGBoost were fitted only on training rows. Test: July–September 2026, excluded from coefficient fitting and regularization selection. This is an exploratory development evaluation: aggregate test metrics were inspected during development, so it is not a pristine independent benchmark. Six sites were excluded from fitting and validation to test geographic transfer: Shimla, Jodhpur, Raipur, Shillong, Bengaluru and Port Blair.

    All 24 sites have nine months of 2025 and nearly nine months of 2026. Raw archive: GFS fixed lead-time series from Open-Meteo Previous Runs, not the near-initialization historical archive. Hours within a day can come from different runs. Live inference uses the latest GFS run and nearest daily lead model, so the live/archive lead alignment is approximate and the published scores are archive scores, not prospective live skill.

    Scope: a representative regional network, not full-grid India, not district-level validation, and not proven nationwide generalization. Some seasons, especially late-year northeast-monsoon conditions, are not covered. Stations and independent observations are needed before safety use.

    Warning-model research · October 1, 2026

    More event detection. Still too many false alarms.

    Separate heavy-rain classifiers and squared-error rainfall models were fitted on 70,368 forecast/reference rows at 24 points from January 2024 through September 24, 2026. Inputs include forecast precipitation, CAPE, humidity, pressure tendencies, wind vectors, elevation and season. Fixed lead-time data begin in 2024, not decades ago.

    These candidates are not the live correction or an operational warning system. 24h and 48h rainfall candidates improve RMSE but worsen MAE versus original v1; the 72h candidate also loses to raw GFS on RMSE. No candidate passed the warning release gate. The live warning stage still abstains. The live rainfall amounts now use the QM+XGBoost/v1 ensemble described above, not these warning-research candidates.

    Splits, release criteria and regional results

    Fit: January 2024–August 2025 at 18 sites. Validation: September 2025–June 2026 at 18 sites. Evaluation: July–September 24, 2026 at 24 sites. Shimla, Jodhpur, Raipur, Shillong, Bengaluru and Port Blair are excluded from fit and validation. This evaluation period was inspected during v1 development, so these are exploratory results, not an untouched independent benchmark. Release criteria were fixed before fitting: ≥20 heavy days, POD ≥60%, false-alarm ratio ≤50%, CSI ≥0.3 and better than raw GFS, with positive probability skill. These development criteria are not an official warning standard.
